We have four Persian couplets (two lines each). Need to see common theme among three and one deviates.

Let's translate roughly.

Option 1: "جهد آن کن تا مگر نامت بماند جاودانی - جاودان کس را نشان باقی نخواهد ماند هرگز"
First line: "Make that effort so that perhaps your name remains eternal." Second line: "Eternal (something) no one will remain as a sign forever." Possibly about striving for lasting fame; but also says eternity won't remain? Might be about futility of seeking immortality? Let's interpret: "Do effort so that your name may stay forever; eternity will not remain for anyone." So concept: striving for lasting reputation, but acknowledging impermanence.

Option 2: "فردا غبار کالبدش در هوا رود - دامن کشان که می رود امروز بر زمین"
First line: "Tomorrow the dust of his body will go into the air." Second: "The one who drags the skirt (perhaps a lover) who goes today on earth." Hard to parse. Might be about mortality, body returning to dust, and someone walking on earth today. Could be about transience of life, mortality.

Option 3: "وانکه دردیش نباشد به جهان هیچ کس است - هیچ کس نیست که او را به جهان دردی نیست"
First line: "And whoever has no pain in the world is nobody." Second: "There is no one who is not in pain in the world." So concept: universal suffering; everyone experiences pain.

Option 4: "هر چیز که شاید و نشاید برود - رفتند و رویم ... and everyone who comes goes" Actually: "هر چیز که شاید و نشاید برود - رفتند و رویم و هر که آید برود". Means: "Everything that may or may not go (be allowed) goes; they have gone and we go, and everyone who comes goes." This seems about impermanence, everything passes, people come and go.

Now find common theme: Options 2,3,4 all talk about transience, mortality, universal suffering, impermanence. Option 1 is about striving for eternal fame, maybe more about ambition and legacy. While others talk about inevitability of death/pain.

Thus option 1 deviates.

Check if any other nuance: Option 2 mentions dust, mortality; Option 3 about pain; Option 4 about everything passing. So yes, 1 is about effort for lasting name, while others talk about inevitability of decay/pain. So answer 1.
